sections.title: Basic Concept: Order and Rank
sections.content: In Order and Ranking, the position (rank) of individuals in a row is determined based on their place or comparisons among them. Questions are usually based on positions from the left and right, the total number of persons, or comparisons such as height or marks.

sections.title: Total Persons When Rank is Given from Both Sides
sections.content:
If a person's position from the left and right is given, the formula to find the total number of persons is:
Total = Rank from left + Rank from right − 1
Example: Rahul is 7th from the left and 5th from the right.
Total persons = 7 + 5 − 1 = 11

sections.title: Finding Rank from the Other Side
sections.content:
If the total number of persons and rank from one side is given, the formula to find the rank from the other side is:
Other side rank = Total − Known rank + 1
Example: There are 20 students in total. Seema is 8th from the left.
Rank from the right = 20 − 8 + 1 = 13

sections.title: Position Interchange
sections.content:
If two persons exchange their positions, their new rank becomes the rank previously held by the other person.
Example: Amit is in the 4th position and Rohit is in the 10th position. If they exchange places, Amit will move to the 10th position and Rohit will move to the 4th position.

sections.title: Comparison of Height / Weight / Marks
sections.content:
If A is taller than B but shorter than C, then the order will be: C > A > B.
In such questions, write the comparisons in order and then identify the tallest or the shortest.

sections.title: Simple Questions with 2–3 Steps
sections.content:
Example: There are 25 students in total. Mohan is 9th from the left.
(1) Rank from the right = 25 − 9 + 1 = 17
(2) If he moves 2 places forward, the new rank = 9 − 2 = 7
Such questions are commonly asked in SSC GD, Railway Group D, and UP Police level exams.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1. Forgetting to subtract 1 while calculating the total.
2. Not adding +1 while finding the rank from the other side.
3. Writing the comparison order incorrectly.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content:
Remember the main formulas:
1. Total = Left rank + Right rank − 1
2. Other side rank = Total − Known rank + 1
For comparison questions, create an order and then solve.

tricks.title: Find Total Persons Instantly
tricks.explanation: Add the ranks from the left and right, then subtract 1.

tricks.title: Shortcut for Other Side Rank
tricks.explanation: Subtract the known rank from the total and add 1.

tricks.title: Position Change Trick
tricks.explanation: If two persons change positions, their ranks are swapped.

tricks.title: Rank When Moving Forward
tricks.explanation: If someone moves forward, their rank from the left decreases.

tricks.title: Rank When Moving Backward
tricks.explanation: If someone moves backward, their rank from the left increases.

tricks.title: Comparison Order Trick
tricks.explanation: Write all names in one line using the > symbol.

tricks.title: Identify Tallest/Shortest
tricks.explanation: In the order, the leftmost is the greatest and the rightmost is the smallest.
tricks.example: C > A > B → C is the tallest

tricks.title: Middle Person
tricks.explanation: If the total number is odd, the middle position is (Total + 1) / 2.

tricks.title: Finding People in Between
tricks.explanation: Number of persons between two ranks = Larger rank − Smaller rank − 1.

tricks.title: Solve a Three-Step Question
tricks.explanation: First find the total, then the other side rank, then apply the change.
tricks.example: Left 7, Right 9 → Total 15 → Find the new rank
